title: Mapping-space descent along spines and increasing unions
statement: Use the local-smallness and universe conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and small simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, mapping spaces and limits of spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $n\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Sp}[n]\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the union of the vertices and the consecutive edges $\{i,i+1\}$, with their degeneracies. For every quasicategory $\mathcal C$, restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Sp}[n],\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence of quasicategories and induces equivalences on all mapping spaces. Let $L_0\subseteq L_1\subseteq\cdots$ be an increasing sequence of small simplicial sets, with degreewise union $L$, and let $F,G:L\to\mathcal C$ be diagrams. Restriction induces a natural equivalence of spaces $$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)}(F,G)\simeq\lim_{n\in\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(L_n,\mathcal C)}(F|_{L_n},G|_{L_n}).$$ This is a homotopy coherent limit, not merely an inverse limit of components, and the equivalence is natural in both diagrams. More generally, if $\mathcal C$ is locally small and $L$ is small, then $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$ is locally small.
